plan.summary: BRO-7245 follow-up: Legally Blonde (2007) Did Not Recoup -> Wait & See, using lead producer Hal Luftig's own figures (around 60% of an $11M capitalization returned on Broadway; $650K weekly running cost).
steps: Freakonomics Radio (Apr 18, 2025): Luftig says the run 'made back only around 60 percent of its $11 million capitalization'; the US tour 'did recoup, and made a profit', London 'did make a small profit', the UK tour 'very profitable'.
BroadwayWorld (Feb 20, 2009), summarizing Variety: Luftig 'notes that Legally Blonde cost $650,000 a week to run'.
60% returned plus continuing tour and licensing income meets Wait & See (50%+ back, later money may still recoup). No source reports full recoupment for the Broadway investors, so not Recouped.

actions.oldValue: Commercial musical at the Palace Theatre (opened Apr 29, 2007; closed Oct 19, 2008 after 595 performances). Lead producer Hal Luftig put the total budget at $12.8M, including about $1.5M for a San Francisco tryout. Grossed about $56M on Broadway and closed without recouping, after grosses fell in fall 2008. No published source says how much of the capitalization came back; a '75% by closing' figure that circulates online traces only to a January 2008 forum projection. The national tour, the West End production and licensing pay royalties to the Broadway company, but no source reports the investors being made whole.
actions.newValue: Commercial musical at the Palace Theatre (opened Apr 29, 2007; closed Oct 19, 2008 after 595 performances). Lead producer Hal Luftig says the Broadway run returned around 60% of its $11M capitalization (his 2006 pre-production budget was $12.8M, including a San Francisco tryout). It cost about $650K a week to run and grossed about $56M. Luftig says the several-year US tour recouped and made a profit, the London production made a small profit and the UK tour that followed was very profitable, and the show is licensed to hundreds of productions a year. Those productions pay royalties to the Broadway company, but no source yet reports the Broadway investors being paid back in full. A '75% by closing' figure that circulates online traces only to a January 2008 forum projection.
